questions.question: What is the outward and visible sign in Baptism?
questions.answer: The outward and visible sign is water, in which candidates are baptized "in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit."

questions.question: What is the inward and spiritual grace given in Baptism?
questions.answer: The inward and spiritual grace is death to sin and new birth to righteousness, through union with Christ in his death and resurrection. I am born a sinner by nature, separated from God. But in Baptism, through faith in Christ and the gift of the Holy Spirit, I am made a member of Christ's Body and adopted as God's child and heir.

questions.question: What is required of you when you come to be baptized?
questions.answer: Two things are required: repentance, in which I turn away from sin; and faith, in which I turn to Jesus Christ as my Savior and Lord and trust the promises that God makes to me in this sacrament.

questions.question: Why is it appropriate to baptize infants?
questions.answer: Because it is a sign of God's promise that they are embraced in the covenant community of Christ's Church. Those who in faith and repentance present infants to be baptized vow to raise them in the knowledge and fear of the Lord, with the expectation that they will one day profess full Christian faith as their own.

questions.question: What signs of the Holy Spirit's work should you hope and pray to see as a result of your Baptism?
questions.answer: I should hope and pray that the Holy Spirit, who indwells me, will help me to be an active member of my Christian community, participate in worship, continually repent and return to God, proclaim the faith, love and serve God and my neighbor, and seek justice and peace.

questions.question: Why did Christ institute the sacrament of Holy Communion?
questions.answer: He instituted it for the continual remembrance of the sacrifice of his atoning death, and to convey the benefits of that sacrifice to us.

questions.question: What is the outward and visible sign in Holy Communion?
questions.answer: The visible sign is bread and wine, which Christ commands us to receive.

questions.question: What is the inward gift signified?
questions.answer: The inward gift signified is the Body and Blood of Christ, which are truly taken and received in the Lord's Supper by faith.

questions.question: What benefits do you receive through partaking of this sacrament?
questions.answer: As my body is nourished by the bread and wine, my soul is strengthened by the Body and Blood of Christ. I receive God's forgiveness, and I am renewed in the love and unity of the Body of Christ, the Church.

questions.question: What is required of you when you come to receive Holy Communion?
questions.answer: I am to examine myself: Do I truly repent of my sins and intend to lead a new life in Christ? Do I have a living faith in God's mercy through Christ and remember his atoning death with a thankful heart? And have I shown love and forgiveness to all people?

questions.question: What is expected of you after partaking in Holy Communion?
questions.answer: I should continue to grow in holiness, avoiding sin, showing love and forgiveness to all, and serving others in gratitude.

questions.question: What is confirmation?
questions.answer: Confirmation is the laying on of the bishop's hands with prayer for strengthening by the Holy Spirit, following a period of catechetical formation. In confirmation, I make a mature confession of faith, publicly renewing the vows and promises made at my Baptism.

questions.question: What grace does God give you in confirmation?
questions.answer: In confirmation, I am further empowered and gifted by the Holy Spirit for daily growth in wisdom, courage, and humility before God in every aspect of my life and work.

questions.question: What is the work of all Christians?
questions.answer: All Christians are to bear witness to Christ in their lives; to care for the poor, strangers, widows, and orphans; and, according to their gifts, to serve Christ in the world and in the Church.

questions.question: What is ordination?
questions.answer: Ordination is the laying on of the bishop's hands with prayer, which confirms the gifts and calling of the candidates, consecrates them, and grants them authority to serve Christ and his Church in the office to which they have been called.

questions.question: What grace does God give in ordination?
questions.answer: In ordination, God conveys the gift of the Holy Spirit for the office and work of the order being conferred.

questions.question: What are the three ordained ministries in the Anglican Church?
questions.answer: The three orders are bishops, priests, and deacons, which we have received from Scripture and the historic Church.

questions.question: What is the work of bishops?
questions.answer: Bishops represent and serve Christ and the Church as chief pastors, catechists, and missionaries in the tradition of the apostles. They are to confirm and ordain, and to guard the faith, unity, and discipline of the Church.

questions.question: What is the work of priests?
questions.answer: Serving Christ with their bishops, priests (or presbyters) nurture God's people through the ministry of Word and Sacrament and pronounce absolution and blessing in God's Name.

questions.question: What is the work of deacons?
questions.answer: Serving Christ under their bishops, deacons care for those in need, assist in public worship, and instruct both young and old in the catechism.

questions.question: What is Christian marriage?
questions.answer: Christian marriage, or Holy Matrimony, is a lifelong covenant between one man and one woman, uniting them in self-giving love, joy, and faithfulness. It is ordained by God for the procreation and spiritual nurture of children, the sanctification of husband and wife, the mutual support of their common life, and the flourishing of family, church, and society.

questions.question: What is signified in marriage?
questions.answer: The union of husband and wife in one flesh signifies the communion between Christ, the heavenly bridegroom, and the Church, his holy bride. Not all are called or able to marry, but all Christians are joined to Christ as members of his Body.

questions.question: What grace does God give in marriage?
questions.answer: In Christian marriage, God unites husband and wife and blesses their common life, that they may grow together in love, wisdom, and godliness, patterned on the sacrificial love of Christ. A Christian marriage embodies this grace in the world, especially through hospitality and care for those who are lonely or in need.

questions.question: What is absolution?
questions.answer: In absolution, a priest, acting under God's authority, pronounces God's forgiveness in response to repentance and confession of sin.

questions.question: What grace does God give to you in absolution?
questions.answer: In absolution, God conveys his pardon through the Cross, removes and cancels my sin, declares me reconciled and at peace with him, and grants me the assurance of his grace and salvation.

questions.question: What is necessary to receive the grace of absolution?
questions.answer: Repentance, in which I intend to resist further sin, accept responsibility for my actions, and endeavor to repair damage I have caused; and faith, by which I thankfully receive God's forgiveness.

questions.question: What is the anointing of the sick?
questions.answer: Through prayer and anointing with oil, the minister invokes God's blessing upon those suffering in body, mind, or spirit.

questions.question: What grace does God give in the anointing of the sick?
questions.answer: God gives healing, strength, and peace, either for recovery from injury or illness, or for perseverance in adversity, especially in preparation for death.

questions.question: What is prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer is turning my heart toward God, to listen and to speak with him.

questions.question: What should you seek in prayer?
questions.answer: In prayer, I should seek not only God's provision for my needs, but fellowship with God, who made me for fellowship with himself.

questions.question: How can you have fellowship with God?
questions.answer: Through the death and resurrection of Jesus, and union with him by the Holy Spirit, I have fellowship with God as his adopted child. I experience this in prayer, worship, God's Word, the sacraments, and Christian community, as I daily follow him by faith.

questions.question: Why should you pray?
questions.answer: I should pray because God calls me to do so, because I was made for fellowship with him, because I need the help of his Holy Spirit, and because he has promised to answer the prayers of his people.

questions.question: What should you pray?
questions.answer: I should pray the Lord's Prayer, the Psalms, the collected prayers of the Church, and my own prayers as the Spirit leads me.

questions.question: When should you pray?
questions.answer: I should pray at regular times throughout each day, with fellow Christians for prayer and worship, and whenever I am aware of a need for God's grace. And I should learn to "pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17) as I grow in the knowledge of God's presence.

questions.question: What is the prayer our Lord Jesus taught his disciples to pray?
questions.answer: The traditional version of the Lord's Prayer is this: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

questions.question: Why should you learn the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: I should learn the Lord's Prayer because Jesus taught it to his disciples as both a practice and a pattern for prayer to God the Father.

questions.question: Why should you practice the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: I should pray the Lord's Prayer regularly because it teaches me to pray as Jesus commanded and to desire what his Father wills.

questions.question: How is the Lord's Prayer a pattern for prayer?
questions.answer: The Lord's Prayer models the primary types of prayer: praise of God, intercession for his rule, petition for his provision and protection, and confession of sins. I should pray regularly in all these ways.

questions.question: What are the parts of the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: The traditional form of the Lord's Prayer begins by addressing God the Father, makes seven petitions, adds a doxology, and concludes with "Amen."

questions.question: Why do we call God "Father"?
questions.answer: We call God "Father" because Jesus teaches his disciples that we are God's children and should call God "our Father."

questions.question: Who are God's children?
questions.answer: All who come to God through faith and Baptism in Christ are adopted as children of God the Father.

questions.question: Why does Jesus teach us to pray "our" Father?
questions.answer: Jesus teaches us always to understand ourselves not only as individuals but as members of God's family of believers, and to pray accordingly.

questions.question: How is God like earthly fathers?
questions.answer: Like all loving and sincere earthly fathers, God loves us in our weakness, provides for our needs, teaches us in our ignorance, and corrects us when we go astray.

questions.question: How is God unlike earthly fathers?
questions.answer: Unlike our natural fathers, our heavenly Father loves us perfectly, is almighty in his care, makes no errors in judgment, and disciplines us only for our good.

questions.question: What is heaven?
questions.answer: Heaven is the realm of God's presence, power, and glory, which exists invisibly alongside this visible realm, and from which God hears the prayers of his children.

questions.question: How does your Father in heaven help you here on earth?
questions.answer: Because God is in all places and knows all things, he hears and answers my prayers, directs my paths, and strengthens me in times of trouble.

questions.question: What is the first petition?
questions.answer: The first petition is "Hallowed be thy Name."

questions.question: What is God's Name?
questions.answer: God's Name reveals who he is—his nature, his character, his power, and his purposes. The Name God reveals to Moses is "I am who I am" or simply "I am" (Exodus 3:6, 14). This Name means that he alone is truly God, he is the source of his own Being, he is holy and just, and he cannot be defined by his creatures.

questions.question: What are some other names for God given in Scripture?
questions.answer: Throughout the Scriptures, God is known as "Lord." Through the Person and ministry of Jesus Christ, God is also revealed to be one God in three Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What does "hallowed" mean?
questions.answer: "Hallowed" means to be treated as holy—set apart, sacred, and glorified.

questions.question: How does God hallow his Name?
questions.answer: God's Name is holy in itself, and God glorifies his Name by saving fallen humanity, by building his Church, and by establishing his kingdom in this world and in the age to come.

questions.question: How can you hallow God's Name?
questions.answer: I can honor God's Name as holy by worshiping him, serving others, and living in loving obedience as his child and a citizen of his kingdom.

questions.question: What is the second petition?
questions.answer: The second petition is "Thy kingdom come."

questions.question: What is God's kingdom?
questions.answer: The kingdom of God is the just and peaceful reign of Jesus Christ over all the world, especially in the lives of his faithful people, through the powerful work of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: When you pray for God's kingdom to come, what are you asking?
questions.answer: I pray that the whole creation may be renewed and restored under its rightful Lord, now in part and fully in the age to come.

questions.question: How does God's kingdom come?
questions.answer: God's kingdom is announced to the people of Israel, arrives in Jesus Christ, and advances through the Church's mission. It will appear in its fullness once Christ returns in glory.

questions.question: How do you live in God's kingdom?
questions.answer: As a citizen of God's kingdom, I am called to live in obedience to God's Word and will, in loving witness and service to others, and in joyful hope of Christ's return.

questions.question: What is the third petition?
questions.answer: The third petition is "Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven."

questions.question: What is God's will?
questions.answer: God's will is to reconcile all things to himself in Jesus Christ and to establish his kingdom on the earth. His will is revealed in the whole of Scripture and especially in Jesus Christ, whom I am called to serve and imitate with my whole life.

questions.question: What do you pray for as you seek God's will?
questions.answer: I pray for God to break the dominion of the world, the flesh, and the devil; to establish justice and thwart the plans of the wicked; to strengthen and direct his Church; and to extend the kingdom of his grace.

questions.question: How can you do God's will?
questions.answer: I can walk in God's will by loving him and my neighbor, and by taking my part in the Church's mission to extend his kingdom in the world.

questions.question: Why do you pray, "on earth as it is in heaven"?
questions.answer: In heaven, God's Name is perfectly hallowed, and his will is perfectly obeyed and fulfilled. I pray for his kingdom to be established fully and his will to be accomplished on earth, that his Name may be perfectly hallowed in all creation.

questions.question: What is the fourth petition?
questions.answer: The fourth petition is "Give us this day our daily bread."

questions.question: Having prayed first for God's glory, kingdom, and will, what do you now pray?
questions.answer: I pray for my needs and those of my brothers and sisters: for daily provision, pardon for sins, and protection from evil.

questions.question: What does "our daily bread" mean?
questions.answer: Daily bread includes all that we need each day for our bodily provision and spiritual nourishment.

questions.question: Why should you pray for daily bread?
questions.answer: God calls me to trust him for the needs of each day, to be concerned for the needs of others, to be content with what I have, and to grow in gratitude for his provision.

questions.question: Why does God give you daily bread?
questions.answer: God gives me daily bread because he is a good and loving Father, who gives good things to all his children, sustains us in life, and desires that we grow daily in his grace.

questions.question: What is the fifth petition?
questions.answer: The fifth petition is "Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us."

questions.question: What are trespasses?
questions.answer: A "trespass" is a sin—a thought, word, or deed which offends God's holy character and violates his Law, missing the mark of his will and expectations.

questions.question: Do you sin against God's Law?
questions.answer: Yes. I, together with all humankind, sin daily against God's Law, in thought, word, and deed, both by what I do and by what I fail to do.

questions.question: What is God's forgiveness?
questions.answer: God's forgiveness is his merciful pardon of sin and removal of the guilt that results from our disobedience.

questions.question: On what basis do you ask forgiveness?
questions.answer: I ask God our loving Father to forgive me through his Son, Jesus Christ, who bore my sins upon the Cross, so that through faith and Baptism I can receive his righteousness.

questions.question: Does God forgive your sins?
questions.answer: Yes. In Christ, God freely forgives the sins of all, including me, who sincerely repent and in true faith turn to him.

questions.question: Why should you forgive others?
questions.answer: I should forgive others because, while I was still a sinner, God forgave me through Jesus Christ. Failing to forgive impedes God's work in my life and gives opportunity to the evil one.

questions.question: How do you forgive others?
questions.answer: Forgiveness is a decision of my will and an attitude of my heart that seeks the good of my neighbor, and chooses not to hold against them the damage they have inflicted. I forgive whether they have asked for forgiveness or not.

questions.question: Will your forgiveness of others always result in reconciliation?
questions.answer: No. Though my decision and desire to forgive may not result in my neighbor's repentance or our reconciliation, I am still called to forgive.

questions.question: What is the sixth petition?
questions.answer: The sixth petition is "And lead us not into temptation."

questions.question: What is temptation?
questions.answer: Temptation is any enticement to turn from faith in God and to violate his commandments.

questions.question: What are the sources of temptation?
questions.answer: I am tempted by the false promises of the world, the selfish desires of my flesh, and the lies of the devil, all of which war against God and my spiritual well-being.

questions.question: What help do you seek from God in the face of temptation?
questions.answer: I ask God to increase my faith to trust him, enliven my conscience to fear him, soften my heart to love him, and strengthen my will to obey him, that I may resist evil and stand in the face of temptation.

questions.question: Does God lead you into temptation?
questions.answer: No. God never tempts anyone, nor is he the cause of any sin; but he does allow me to be tested so that I may grow in faith and obedience.

questions.question: What are ways to guard against temptation?
questions.answer: As I abide in Christ, I can guard against temptation by praying for protection and strength, confessing my sins, recalling God's Word, avoiding tempting situations, and seeking the support of fellow Christians.

questions.question: How can the Church help you to resist temptation?
questions.answer: In the fellowship of Christ's Body, I can find companionship when I am lonely or vulnerable, support to resist ungodly influence, wisdom to guard me from folly, exhortation to grow in holiness, and discipline to correct me when I fall into error.

questions.question: What is the seventh petition?
questions.answer: The seventh petition is "But deliver us from evil."

questions.question: What is evil?
questions.answer: Evil is the willful perversion of God's will. Evil defies God's holiness, violates his Law, enslaves us to sin, and mars his good creation.

questions.question: If God is good, why does he permit evil?
questions.answer: God created rational creatures free to love, obey, and worship him, but we have used our freedom to reject his love, rebel against him, and choose evil. Yet no evil can thwart God's purposes, and he is able to use evil to bring about even greater good.

questions.question: Is God responsible for evil?
questions.answer: No. The sinful choices of his creatures do not implicate God in evil in any way.

questions.question: Did evil exist before the human race embraced it?
questions.answer: Yes. Satan had already opposed God and chosen evil when he tempted Adam and Eve.

questions.question: What are Satan and his demons?
questions.answer: Demons, of whom Satan is chief, are fallen angels. Satan rebelled against God and led other angels to follow him. They now cause spiritual and sometimes physical harm to mortals, and they sow lies that lead to confusion, despair, sin, and death.

questions.question: How did Satan and his angels turn to evil?
questions.answer: Satan and his angels were overcome by envy and pride and rebelled against God.

questions.question: What are angels?
questions.answer: Angels are rational, spiritual beings created by God. God's holy angels joyfully serve him in heavenly worship, and God appoints them to act as messengers, bringing words of guidance and assurance to the faithful, and assisting and protecting them.

questions.question: How does God overcome evil in this world?
questions.answer: God has triumphed over all the powers of evil through the death, resurrection, and ascension of his Son, Jesus Christ. God will finally destroy all evil, including death, at the end of the age.

questions.question: How does God redeem evil?
questions.answer: Though disaster, disease, death, and the evil deeds of his creatures may cause great harm and suffering, the almighty and all-wise God can use them to bring about his good purposes, both in the world and in my life.

questions.question: From what evil do you seek to be delivered?
questions.answer: I seek to be delivered from my own fallen inclination toward evil. I also seek God's deliverance from the devil; from the dangers of the day and night; from sorrow, sickness, and horror; from injustice and oppression; and from everlasting damnation.

questions.question: How does God deliver you from evil?
questions.answer: Jesus has conquered the dominion of darkness and now grants me victory over sin and evil through the Holy Spirit. He transforms my mind and heart to see and oppose evil, and gives me the power to overcome it. He gives me strength to endure my trials gracefully and may even remove them from me.

questions.question: What is the doxology of the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: The doxology often added to the Lord's Prayer is "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen" (Matthew 6:13). A doxology is a short phrase or hymn giving glory to God.

questions.question: What does "kingdom, power, and glory" mean?
questions.answer: Mirroring the first half of the Lord's Prayer, the Church rejoices that God is already reigning over all creation, working out his holy will, and hallowing his Name in earth and heaven.

questions.question: Why do you end the Lord's Prayer by saying "Amen"?
questions.answer: By saying "Amen," which means "so be it," I declare my agreement with the prayer. I unite with the faithful, and together we pray as Jesus commanded, believing that our petitions please the Father, and trusting that he will hear and answer us.

sections.section: A Rule of Prayer: Scripture, Prayer, and Worship

questions.question: What is a "rule" of prayer?
questions.answer: A rule of prayer is a regular discipline by which I cultivate a life of prayer and grow to love and glorify God more fully.

questions.question: What can hinder your regular prayers?
questions.answer: My prayers may be hindered by many things, such as lethargy or loss, selfishness or sin, distractions or difficulties, or seasons of spiritual dryness. With God's help, a rule of prayer strengthens me to overcome all these.

questions.question: What nurtures a fruitful life of prayer?
questions.answer: My life of prayer is fed by the regular reading of Scripture, practice of personal prayer, and corporate worship of God. The ancient threefold rule of the Church encourages weekly Communion, the Daily Office, and private devotions to shape this way of life.

questions.question: How should the Holy Scriptures shape your daily life?
questions.answer: I should "hear them, read, mark, learn, and inwardly digest them" that by the sustaining power of God's Word, I may grow in grace and hold fast to the hope given to me in Jesus Christ.

questions.question: How should you "hear" the Bible?
questions.answer: I should hear the Bible through regular participation in the Church's worship, in which I join in reciting Scripture, hear it read and prayed, and listen to its truth proclaimed.

questions.question: How should you "read" the Bible?
questions.answer: I should read the Bible daily, following the Church's set readings (lectionaries) or following a pattern of my own choosing.

questions.question: How should you "mark" passages of Scripture?
questions.answer: I should study the Bible attentively, noting key verses and themes, as well as connections between passages in the Old and New Testaments. I should study on my own and with other Christians, using trustworthy commentaries and other resources to grasp the full meaning of God's Word.

questions.question: How should you "learn" the Bible?
questions.answer: I should seek to know the whole sweep of Scripture and to memorize key passages for my own spiritual growth and for sharing with others.

questions.question: How should you "inwardly digest" Scripture?
questions.answer: I should meditate on Scripture and let it shape my thoughts and prayers. As I absorb Scripture, it deepens my knowledge of God, becomes the lens through which I understand my life and the world around me, and guides my attitudes and actions.

questions.question: Are there different ways to pray?
questions.answer: Yes. Prayer can be private or public, liturgical or extemporaneous, spoken or silent.

questions.question: What types of prayer are in the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: The Lord's Prayer includes praise, petition, intercession, and confession to God.

questions.question: What is praise?
questions.answer: In praise, I glorify and adore God for his holiness, his sovereign rule over all, and his salvation given in Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What is petition?
questions.answer: In petition, I make requests to God on my own behalf for his provision and protection.

questions.question: What is intercession?
questions.answer: In intercession, I make requests to God on behalf of others, the Church, and the world.

questions.question: What is confession?
questions.answer: In confession, I acknowledge my sins in repentance before God and receive his forgiveness.

questions.question: What types of prayer are not included in the Lord's Prayer?
questions.answer: Other types of prayer are thanksgiving, by which I give thanks to God for his providential goodness and answers to my prayers; and oblation, by which I offer to him all that I am and all that I do.

questions.question: With what attitude should you pray?
questions.answer: I should pray with humility, love, and a ready openness to hear and do God's will.

questions.question: What prayers should you learn as a part of your rule of prayer?
questions.answer: After learning the Lord's Prayer, I should next aim to learn certain psalms (such as Psalms 23, 51, 95, 100, 150) and prayers from the Daily Office. These prayers will ground me in the Christian tradition of prayer and teach me how to pray in my own words.

questions.question: What should you remember when prayers seem to go unanswered?
questions.answer: I should be certain that God always hears my prayers and answers them by his wisdom, in his own time and manner, for my good, and for his glory.

questions.question: How should you pray in times of suffering?
questions.answer: I should pray trusting in the sufficiency of God's grace and in joyful assurance that "suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not put us to shame."

questions.question: What is liturgy?
questions.answer: Liturgy is an established pattern or form for the worship of God by God's people. The liturgy leads us in the remembrance of God's mighty acts and unites us in grateful response.

questions.question: Why do Anglicans worship with a structured liturgy?
questions.answer: Anglicans worship with a structured liturgy because it embodies biblical patterns of worship, fosters reverence and love for God, deepens faith in Jesus Christ, and is in continuity with the practices of Israel and the Early Church.

questions.question: Does structured liturgy inhibit sincere and vibrant worship?
questions.answer: No. A structured liturgy provides sincere worshipers biblical language and forms that train our hearts for worship. Liturgy enables us to worship God joyfully and with one voice.

questions.question: What is the role of Scripture in the Prayer Book?
questions.answer: The Book of Common Prayer is saturated with the Scriptures, organizing and orchestrating them for worship. It helps us to pray together in words God himself has given us, with order, beauty, joy, deep devotion, and great dignity.

questions.question: How does the Book of Common Prayer organize corporate worship?
questions.answer: The Prayer Book orders our daily, weekly, and seasonal prayer and worship. It also provides liturgies for significant events of life.

questions.question: What is the Daily Office?
questions.answer: The Daily Office includes the services of Morning and Evening Prayer. In them we confess our sins and receive absolution, hear God's Word and praise him with psalms, and offer the Church's thanksgivings and prayers.

questions.question: How is the Daily Office observed?
questions.answer: The Daily Office is primarily designed for corporate prayer. It may also be used by individuals or families, in public or in private, in whole or in part.

questions.question: Why do we pray the Daily Office?
questions.answer: We pray the Daily Office because, by it, we learn the Scriptures, join with the Church in prayer, mark our days with praise to God, and sanctify our time.

questions.question: What is a rule of life?
questions.answer: A rule of life is a discipline by which I order my worship, work, and leisure as a pleasing sacrifice to God.

questions.question: Why do you need a rule of life?
questions.answer: I need a rule of life because my fallen nature is disordered, distracted, and self-centered. A rule of life helps me to resist sin and establish godly habits, through which the Holy Spirit will increasingly conform me to the image of Christ.

questions.question: What is included in a rule of life?
questions.answer: In addition to Scripture, prayer, and worship, a rule of life includes witness, service, self-denial, and faithful stewardship of my time, money, and possessions.

questions.question: Why is prayer an essential part of a rule of life?
questions.answer: Through prayer, I rely upon God for strength, wisdom, and humility to sustain and guide me in my rule of life. Without the love of God and the power of his Spirit, I will not attain to the fullness of Christ.

questions.question: Recite the Ten Commandments.
questions.answer:
1. I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods but me.
2. You shall not make for yourself any idol.
3. You shall not take the Name of the Lord your God in vain.
4. Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
5. Honor your father and your mother.
6. You shall not murder.
7. You shall not commit adultery.
8. You shall not steal.
9. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
10. You shall not covet.

questions.question: What are the Ten Commandments?
questions.answer: The Ten Commandments are a summary and outline of God's Law.

questions.question: What is God's Law?
questions.answer: God's Law (Hebrew, torah: "instruction") is God's direct pronouncement of his will, both for our good and for his glory.

questions.question: When did God give his Law?
questions.answer: After delivering his people Israel from slavery in Egypt, God established a covenant with them by giving them his Law through Moses.

questions.question: How did Jesus summarize God's Law?
questions.answer: Jesus summarized God's Law by saying: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets."

questions.question: How did Jesus fulfill God's Law?
questions.answer: For our sake, Jesus fulfilled God's Law by teaching it perfectly, submitting to it wholly, and dying as an atoning sacrifice for our disobedience.

questions.question: How can you obey God's Law?
questions.answer: As I trust in Jesus' fulfillment of the Law for me and live in the power of the Holy Spirit, God grants me grace to love and obey his Law.

questions.question: Why are you not able to do this perfectly?
questions.answer: Sin has corrupted human nature, inclining me to resist God, to ignore his will, and to care more for myself than for my neighbors. However, God has begun and will continue his transforming work in me, and will fully conform me to Christ at the end of the age.

questions.question: How should you understand the Ten Commandments?
questions.answer: I should understand them as God's righteous rules for life in his kingdom: basic standards for loving God and my neighbor. In upholding them, I bear witness with the Church to God's righteousness and his will for a just society.

questions.question: How do the Ten Commandments help you to resist evil?
questions.answer: They teach me that God judges the corrupt affections of this fallen world, the cruel strategies of the devil, and the sinful desires of my own heart; and they teach me to renounce them.

questions.question: How do the Ten Commandments help you to grow in likeness to Christ?
questions.answer: They reveal my sin in the light of God's righteousness, guide me to Christ, and teach me what is pleasing to God.

questions.question: How should you keep the Ten Commandments?
questions.answer: Because they both contain God's prohibitions against evil and direct me toward his good will, I should both repent when I disobey them and seek by his grace to live according to them.

questions.question: What is the first commandment?
questions.answer: The first commandment is "I am the Lord your God. . . . You shall have no other gods before me."

questions.question: What does it mean that the Lord is your God?
questions.answer: It means that I have faith that the God of the Bible is the only true God and that I entrust myself to him wholly.

questions.question: What does it mean to have no other gods?
questions.answer: It means that there should be nothing in my life more important than God and obeying his will. I should worship him only and love, revere, and trust him above all else.

questions.question: Why are you tempted to worship other things instead of God?
questions.answer: I am tempted because my sinful heart seeks my own desires above all else and pursues those things which falsely promise to fulfill them.

questions.question: How are you tempted to worship other gods?
questions.answer: I am tempted to trust in myself, my pleasures, my possessions, my relationships, and my success, wrongly believing that they will bring me happiness, security, and meaning. I am also tempted to believe superstitions and false religious claims, and to reject God's call to worship him alone.

questions.question: Can you worship and serve God perfectly?
questions.answer: No. Only our Lord Jesus Christ worshiped and served God perfectly; but I can seek to imitate Christ, knowing that my worship and service are acceptable to God through him.

questions.question: What is the second commandment?
questions.answer: The second commandment is "You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. You shall not bow down to them or serve them."

questions.question: What does the second commandment mean?
questions.answer: God's people are neither to worship man-made images of God or of other gods nor to make such images for the purpose of worshiping them.

questions.question: How did Israel break the first two commandments?
questions.answer: Israel neglected God's Law, worshiped the gods of the nations around them, and brought images of these gods (idols) into God's temple, thus corrupting his worship.

questions.question: Why did the nations make such images?
questions.answer: Israel's neighbors worshiped and served false gods by means of idols, believing they could manipulate these counterfeit gods for their own benefit.

questions.question: Are all images wrong?
questions.answer: No. God forbade the making of idols and the worship of images, yet commanded carvings and pictures for the tabernacle depicting creation. Christians are free to make images—including images of Jesus and the saints—as long as they do not worship them or use them superstitiously.

questions.question: Are idols always images?
questions.answer: No. Anything can become an idol if I look to it for salvation from my sin or comfort amid my circumstances. If I place my ultimate hope in anything but God, it is an idol.

questions.question: What does the second commandment teach you about hope?
questions.answer: It teaches me that my ultimate hope is in God alone, for he alone is God and he made me. I must not look for salvation and fulfillment in myself, another person, my wealth or occupation or status, or any created thing. Only in God will I find perfect love and fulfillment.

questions.question: How was Jesus tempted to break the first two commandments?
questions.answer: Satan tempted Jesus to bow down and worship him, promising him an earthly kingdom without the pain of the Cross. Instead, Jesus served and worshiped God faithfully and perfectly all his life, and calls us to do the same.

questions.question: How will idolatry affect you?
questions.answer: If I worship and serve idols, I will become like them, empty and alienated from God, who alone can make me whole.

questions.question: What is the third commandment?
questions.answer: The third commandment is "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain."

questions.question: Why is God's Name sacred?
questions.answer: God's Name reveals who he is—his nature, his character, his power, and his purposes. All forms of God's Name are holy.

questions.question: What does it mean to take God's Name "in vain"?
questions.answer: "Vain" means empty, meaningless, and of no account. To take God's Name in vain is to treat it as such.

questions.question: How can you avoid taking God's Name in vain?
questions.answer: Because I love him, I should use God's Name with reverence, not carelessly or profanely.

questions.question: How might you use God's Name profanely?
questions.answer: By the unholy use of God's holy Name, especially through perjury, blasphemy, and attributing to God any falsehood, heresy, or evil deed, as if he had authorized or approved them.

questions.question: How might you use God's Name carelessly?
questions.answer: Cursing, magic, broken vows, false piety, manipulation of others, and hypocrisy all cheapen God's Name. These treat God's Name as empty of the reality for which it stands.
questions.articlesText: As we confess that vain and rash Swearing is forbidden Christian men by our Lord Jesus Christ, and James his Apostle, so we judge, that Christian Religion doth not prohibit, but that a man may swear when the Magistrate requireth, in a cause of faith and charity, so it be done according to the Prophet's teaching in justice, judgment, and truth.

questions.question: How can you honor and love God's Name?
questions.answer: I honor and love God's Name, in which I was baptized, by keeping my vows and promises, by worshiping him in truth and holiness, and by invoking his Name reverently and responsibly.

questions.question: What is the fourth commandment?
questions.answer: The fourth commandment is "Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy."

questions.question: What does it mean to keep the Sabbath day holy?
questions.answer: "Sabbath" is from the Hebrew shabbath, which means "rest." "Holy" means "set apart" for God's purposes. God commanded Israel to set apart each seventh day, following six days of work, for rest and worship.

questions.question: Why was Israel to rest on the Sabbath?
questions.answer: Israel was called to rest in remembrance that God had freed them from slavery and that God rested from his work of creation, bringing joyful balance and rhythm to life, work, and worship.

questions.question: How did Jesus teach us to keep the Sabbath?
questions.answer: As Lord of the Sabbath, Jesus taught us to keep it not merely as a duty, but as a gift of God to be received with joy and extended to others through acts of love and hospitality.

questions.question: How do Christians keep the Sabbath?
questions.answer: Christians keep the Sabbath by gathering for worship on the Lord's Day, the first day of the week, in celebration of Christ's resurrection. On this day we rest from our ordinary labors and devote ourselves to worship, fellowship, works of mercy, and renewal in Christ.

questions.question: What is the fifth commandment?
questions.answer: The fifth commandment is "Honor your father and your mother."

questions.question: What does it mean to honor your father and mother?
questions.answer: It means to love, respect, and obey my parents, to care for them when they are in need, and to receive their godly instruction with gratitude.

questions.question: Why are you to honor your father and mother?
questions.answer: God has set parents in authority over their children for their good. By honoring my parents, I honor God's order and receive his promised blessing.

questions.question: What does the fifth commandment teach about authority?
questions.answer: The fifth commandment teaches me to respect and submit to all God-given authority: parents, teachers, employers, civic leaders, and church authorities. It calls those in authority to exercise it wisely and humbly, for the good of those in their care.

questions.question: What is the sixth commandment?
questions.answer: The sixth commandment is "You shall not murder."

questions.question: What does the sixth commandment prohibit?
questions.answer: This commandment prohibits the unjust taking of human life. Because every human being is made in the image of God, human life is sacred and must be protected and preserved.

questions.question: How does Jesus interpret the sixth commandment?
questions.answer: Jesus teaches that this commandment forbids not only the act of murder but also the anger, hatred, and contempt that give rise to it. He calls us to be reconciled to one another.

questions.question: What does the sixth commandment require of you?
questions.answer: This commandment requires me to value and protect human life—including my own—to show mercy to those in need, and to pursue peace and reconciliation.

questions.question: What is the seventh commandment?
questions.answer: The seventh commandment is "You shall not commit adultery."

questions.question: What does the seventh commandment prohibit?
questions.answer: This commandment prohibits all sexual activity outside of marriage between a man and a woman, as God has ordained it.

questions.question: How does Jesus interpret the seventh commandment?
questions.answer: Jesus teaches that this commandment forbids not only the act of adultery but also lustful thoughts and desires. He calls us to purity of heart.

questions.question: What does the seventh commandment require of you?
questions.answer: This commandment requires me to honor marriage as a sacred covenant, to maintain sexual purity in thought and deed, and to show respect for the dignity of all persons as created in God's image.

questions.question: What is the eighth commandment?
questions.answer: The eighth commandment is "You shall not steal."

questions.question: What does the eighth commandment prohibit?
questions.answer: This commandment prohibits taking what belongs to another, whether by theft, fraud, or exploitation.

questions.question: What does the eighth commandment require of you?
questions.answer: This commandment requires me to respect the property of others, to be honest in my dealings, to share generously with those in need, and to work faithfully for my living.

questions.question: What is the ninth commandment?
questions.answer: The ninth commandment is "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."

questions.question: What does the ninth commandment prohibit?
questions.answer: This commandment prohibits lying, slander, gossip, deception, and all forms of dishonesty that harm our neighbor.

questions.question: What does the ninth commandment require of you?
questions.answer: This commandment requires me to speak the truth in love, to defend the reputation of my neighbor, and to put the most charitable interpretation on the actions of others.

questions.question: What is the tenth commandment?
questions.answer: The tenth commandment is "You shall not covet."

questions.question: What does the tenth commandment prohibit?
questions.answer: This commandment prohibits the sinful desire to have what belongs to another. It addresses the heart from which all other sins arise.

questions.question: How does the tenth commandment reveal the nature of God's Law?
questions.answer: It shows that God's Law addresses not just outward actions but the desires and motivations of the heart. All sins begin with disordered desire.

questions.question: What does the tenth commandment require of you?
questions.answer: This commandment requires me to cultivate contentment with God's provision, to rejoice in the blessings of others, and to desire only what is rightfully mine.

questions.question: How do the commandments relate to love?
questions.answer: The first four commandments teach us to love God with all our heart, soul, mind, and strength; the last six teach us to love our neighbor as ourselves. All the commandments flow from and lead to love.

questions.question: How does Christ fulfill the Law for you?
questions.answer: Christ fulfilled the Law by obeying it perfectly in our place and by dying to atone for our disobedience. United to him by faith, I am credited with his righteousness and empowered by his Spirit to walk in his ways.

questions.question: What is the place of the Law in the Christian life?
questions.answer: The Law reveals my sin and my need for Christ; it guides me in the way of holiness; and it reflects God's good and righteous character. As I walk in the Spirit, I fulfill the Law's intent through love.

questions.question: How does the Holy Spirit help you to keep the commandments?
questions.answer: The Holy Spirit writes God's Law on my heart, transforms my desires, convicts me of sin, and empowers me to walk in obedience as a child of God.

questions.question: How does following the commandments benefit your neighbor?
questions.answer: By keeping the commandments, I honor God's ordering of society, protect the vulnerable, maintain trust and truthfulness, and demonstrate the love of Christ in my daily life.

questions.question: What does the Law teach you about the character of God?
questions.answer: The Law reveals that God is holy, just, and good. His commands reflect his nature: he is truthful, faithful, loving, and righteous, and he calls his people to reflect these qualities.

questions.question: How does the Law point you to the Gospel?
questions.answer: The Law shows me my sin and my inability to save myself, driving me to Christ, who alone fulfills the Law and offers forgiveness and new life by grace through faith.

questions.question: What is the relationship between law and grace?
questions.answer: Grace does not abolish the Law but fulfills it. In Christ, I am freed from the condemnation of the Law and enabled by the Holy Spirit to live in glad obedience to God's commands.

questions.question: What is meant by the fear of God in relation to the commandments?
questions.answer: The fear of God means living in reverent awe of him, taking his commands seriously, hating sin because it offends his holiness, and trusting in his mercy for forgiveness when I fall short.

questions.question: What is the relationship between keeping the commandments and eternal life?
questions.answer: Eternal life is a gift of God's grace, received through faith in Jesus Christ alone—not earned by keeping the commandments. Nevertheless, obedience is the fruit of saving faith, and those who love Christ will keep his commandments.

questions.question: How should you respond when you fail to keep the commandments?
questions.answer: I should confess my sin, receive God's forgiveness through Christ, and by the power of the Holy Spirit seek to amend my life and walk more faithfully in obedience.

questions.question: How does Jesus' Sermon on the Mount relate to the Ten Commandments?
questions.answer: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus unfolds the full meaning of the commandments, showing that they address the heart as well as outward actions, and calling his disciples to a righteousness that exceeds mere external compliance.

questions.question: What do the commandments teach you about human dignity?
questions.answer: The commandments protect human dignity by forbidding actions that harm, devalue, or dehumanize others. They affirm that every person, made in God's image, deserves honor, justice, and care.

questions.question: How are you to use the commandments in your daily life?
questions.answer: I should use the commandments as a mirror to examine my heart and conduct, as a guide for living in a way pleasing to God, and as a reminder of my need for Christ's grace and the Holy Spirit's power.

questions.question: What is the relationship between love and the commandments?
questions.answer: Love is both the fulfillment of the commandments and the motive for keeping them. Because God first loved me, I love him and my neighbor, and this love expresses itself in obedience to his commands.

questions.question: How do the commandments shape the community of the Church?
questions.answer: The commandments shape the Church as a community of love, truth, and justice, in which members honor God, respect one another, speak truthfully, and care for the vulnerable—bearing witness to God's kingdom.

questions.question: How do the commandments relate to Christian witness in the world?
questions.answer: By living in accordance with the commandments, I bear witness to the goodness and justice of God before a watching world, showing that the Gospel transforms not only the heart but all of life.

questions.question: How does keeping the commandments reflect the image of God?
questions.answer: As I grow in obedience to God's Law by the Holy Spirit, I am being restored to the image of God in which I was created—reflecting his justice, love, holiness, and truth more fully.

questions.question: What is the greatest commandment?
questions.answer: Jesus declared the greatest commandment to be: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." The second is like it: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."

questions.question: What does it mean to love God with all your heart, soul, and mind?
questions.answer: It means that my devotion, trust, and obedience belong wholly to God. I am to seek him above all things, worship him with my whole being, and allow nothing to displace him as my highest love.

questions.question: What does it mean to love your neighbor as yourself?
questions.answer: It means to care for the wellbeing of others as genuinely as I care for my own—seeking their good, meeting their needs, treating them with justice and compassion, and forgiving them as I have been forgiven.

questions.question: Who is your neighbor?
questions.answer: My neighbor is anyone in need of help or care, regardless of race, religion, or background. Jesus' parable of the Good Samaritan teaches that we are to show mercy to all people.

questions.question: How does love for God lead to love for neighbor?
questions.answer: Because God is love and I am filled with his Spirit, his love overflows in me toward others. As I am loved by God, I am freed and empowered to love my neighbor sacrificially.

questions.question: How does Jesus demonstrate the greatest commandment?
questions.answer: Jesus demonstrates perfect love for the Father through his entire life of obedience, and perfect love for his neighbor through his self-giving death on the Cross for our sins.

questions.question: What is the new commandment Jesus gives?
questions.answer: Jesus gives a new commandment: "Love one another as I have loved you." This love—selfless, sacrificial, and Christlike—is to be the mark of his disciples.

questions.question: How does Christian love differ from worldly love?
questions.answer: Christian love is not merely a feeling or preference but a deliberate act of will and service, patterned on Christ's own love—it loves even enemies, forgives those who wrong us, and seeks the good of others before our own.

questions.question: What does love require in relation to justice?
questions.answer: Genuine love requires seeking justice for the vulnerable and oppressed. Love without justice is incomplete; true love acts to protect the weak, defend the innocent, and uphold what is right.

questions.question: What does love require in relation to truth?
questions.answer: True love speaks the truth, even when difficult. Love never rejoices in falsehood but always upholds what is right, honest, and honorable.

questions.question: How does love for God transform your loves for earthly things?
questions.answer: When I love God supremely, all other loves are rightly ordered. I love family, friends, work, and creation as gifts of God rather than ends in themselves, and I hold them with an open hand.

questions.question: What does the commandment to love require regarding enemies?
questions.answer: Jesus calls me to love my enemies, pray for those who persecute me, and do good to those who hate me—overcoming evil with good.

questions.question: How does love motivate service and stewardship?
questions.answer: Because I love God and my neighbor, I am moved to serve others generously, to care for creation faithfully, and to use my time, talents, and possessions as a steward of God's gifts.

questions.question: How is love perfected in the Christian life?
questions.answer: Love is perfected through abiding in Christ, receiving his love in prayer and sacrament, obeying his commands, and growing daily in the fruit of the Holy Spirit, until love becomes the ruling disposition of my heart.

questions.question: What is the relationship between love and eternal life?
questions.answer: Eternal life is to know and love God in Christ—not merely to exist forever, but to dwell in the fullness of God's love throughout eternity. Love now is a foretaste of the love that will fill the age to come.

questions.question: How does love for God motivate evangelism and mission?
questions.answer: Because I love God and my neighbor, I desire that all people come to know the saving love of God in Christ. This compels me to share the Gospel, to pray for the lost, and to participate in the Church's mission to the world.

questions.question: What is the fruit of love in the community of the Church?
questions.answer: Love in the Church produces unity, mutual care, forgiveness, hospitality, and shared mission. It is the mark by which the world knows we belong to Jesus Christ.

questions.question: How is love expressed in worship?
questions.answer: In worship, my love for God overflows in praise, thanksgiving, confession, and self-offering. Worship is love responding to Love—the creature adoring the Creator who is infinitely worthy.

questions.question: What is the source of Christian love?
questions.answer: The source of Christian love is God himself. The Holy Spirit pours God's love into my heart so that I am able to love God and my neighbor in ways that transcend my natural capacity.

questions.question: How does love overcome sin?
questions.answer: Where love grows, sin diminishes. As the Holy Spirit fills me with love for God and neighbor, the power of sinful desires is broken, and I am freed to live in obedience, holiness, and joy.

questions.question: What does it mean to love God with all your strength?
questions.answer: It means to devote my entire capacity—physical, material, vocational—to God's service. Nothing I have is my own; all is a stewardship from God, to be used in love for his glory and my neighbor's good.

questions.question: How does love shape your understanding of freedom?
questions.answer: True freedom is not the license to do whatever I wish, but the liberation to live as I was created—in love for God and neighbor. Christ sets me free from the bondage of sin so that I may freely and joyfully love.

sections.section: Justification and Sanctification: Living in Forgiveness and Healing

questions.question: What is justification?
questions.answer: Justification is God's act of declaring sinners righteous in his sight through faith in Jesus Christ. It is a free gift of his grace, not earned by any works of my own, but received by faith alone on account of Christ alone.

questions.question: What is sanctification?
questions.answer: Sanctification is the ongoing work of God's Holy Spirit transforming me into the likeness of Jesus Christ. It begins at the new birth and continues throughout life, as I grow in holiness, resist sin, and bear the fruit of the Spirit.

questions.question: How are justification and sanctification related?
questions.answer: Justification and sanctification are distinct but inseparable. Justification is the foundation; it declares me righteous before God. Sanctification is the fruit; it makes me righteous in life. Both are works of God's grace.

questions.question: What is the assurance of salvation?
questions.answer: The assurance of salvation is the confidence that, because I trust in Christ, I am forgiven, accepted, and held securely in God's love. This assurance is given by the Holy Spirit through the Word and sacraments.

questions.question: How does God heal the wounds of sin?
questions.answer: God heals the wounds of sin through the forgiveness of Christ, the renewing work of the Holy Spirit, the fellowship of the Church, the ministry of the Word and sacraments, prayer, and the pastoral care of the community.

questions.question: What does it mean to live in forgiveness?
questions.answer: To live in forgiveness means to rest daily in God's pardon of my sins through Christ, to confess my ongoing failures, to receive his continual cleansing, and to extend to others the same forgiveness I have received.

questions.question: What is the role of the community in sanctification?
questions.answer: The Church is a community of grace in which we grow together in holiness. Through worship, fellowship, accountability, mutual encouragement, and the sacraments, we help one another to pursue holiness and bear one another's burdens.

questions.question: How do you persevere in the Christian life?
questions.answer: I persevere by abiding in Christ through prayer and Scripture, by remaining in the fellowship of the Church, by confessing my sins and receiving forgiveness, and by trusting in the faithfulness of God who has begun a good work in me and will bring it to completion.

questions.question: What is glorification?
questions.answer: Glorification is the final stage of salvation, when Christ returns and transforms my body to be like his glorious resurrected body, completing the redemption of the whole person—soul and body—to dwell forever in God's presence.

questions.question: What is the hope of the Christian?
questions.answer: The hope of the Christian is the return of Jesus Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and the renewal of all things—the fullness of God's kingdom when all sorrow, sin, and death will be no more, and God will dwell with his people forever.

questions.question: How does the hope of glory shape your life today?
questions.answer: The hope of glory frees me from fear of death, gives me strength to endure suffering, motivates me to live in holiness, and inspires me to share the Gospel, knowing that this present life is preparation for an eternal life of joy in Christ.

questions.question: What is the chief end of man?
questions.answer: The chief end of man is to glorify God and to enjoy him forever—to know him, love him, worship him, and serve him in this life, and to dwell with him in perfect joy in the life to come.
